newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on continued rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on continued rebound.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed up on Monday on a continuation of last Friday's rebound with domestic investors, encouraged by rises on the A share market, dominating trading, traders said.
The index rose 1.210 points or 1.96 percent to 62.888 points, on volume of 20 million shares worth $8.2 million against $6.5 million on Friday.

Brokers said the index was pushed up mainly by speculative buying on index-weighted shares by domestic institutions that were encouraged by the rebound in the A shares, with most overseas investors staying on the sidelines.

"Obviously there are some institutions which do not want the market to fall because they hold large positions," one broker said. "But overseas investors are staying on the sidelines, which limits the potential for rises."
"The index will consolidate around 63 points tomorrow with investors mixed about the market trend," a second broker said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 34 up, four flat and five down.
Newcomer clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai was the star on today's heaviest trade supported by institutions that hold large position in the stock, brokers said.
It jumped $0.032 or its limit-up of 10 percent to $0.356 on volume of 4.8 million shares.
Chlor Alkali performed strongly, rising $0.024 or 8.51 percent to $0.306 on volume of 1.2 million shares.
meanwhile, Shanghai's A share market was firm on expectations of credit-easing measures emerging from a national meeting of bankers in Beijing which began today, brokers said.
The A index rose 11.402 points or 1.19 percent to 970.315 points, on volume of 353.5 million shares worth 3.1 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index gained 18.229 points or 0.75 percent to 2456.469 points.
Eastern China Computer was the star on speculative buying, soaring 10 percent to its limit-up of 10.12 yuan on volume of 1.6 million shares.
